title: Rooming on the road with Dizzy, Parker and Sarah; Fats plays just like Dizzy
summary: Players doubled up in hotels, and Dizzy announced the new trumpeter played just like him; Navarro proved an excellent replacement.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I remember when Dizzy was with the band, he came in the hotel one night, and I think... A lot of times, Dizzy and I would room together. As a matter of fact, different guys at different times would get a room together for some reason or another. Either your money was short or they didn't have that many rooms, so you'd double up. In that way, I shared rooms with Dizzy, Charlie Parker, or any number of the other members of the band, including I even shared a room with Sarah Vaughan. It was a very platonic relationship, because Sarah's the kind of person that if she didn't want to be bothered, you had a good fight on your hands. Sarah could go... As I said, she could be just like one of the guys, and the guys did not bother her.

But Dizzy came in the room one night -- I think we were rooming together. He made this expression. He said, 'Man, I got a trumpet player that I recommended to come in the band, and he plays just like me!' Everybody was elated. I had never heard of Fats before.

But Fats came in the band, and actually, except for the leadership of Dizzy, as far as the band was concerned he wasn't really missed that much in his playing, because Fats was really one hell of a player. As far as playing the solos and the section thing was concerned, he was an excellent replacement.
